generation: Speedmax CF Disc (2021 on; one-piece carbon cockpit from mid-2024)
identify: The more affordable disc Speedmax with an ordinary front end: a standard 1-1/8 in steerer, a Canyon base bar, and Profile Design brackets, risers and extensions. Bikes from 2021 to mid-2024 have Canyon's alloy V21 aero stem with the HB0053 base bar (the V21 stem was recalled for bikes sold May 2017 to July 2024). From mid-2024 the bar and stem are one carbon piece (CP0041). Not the CFR or CF SLX: those have Canyon's own spacer column under the pads.

cockpit.steerer: 1-1/8 in fork steerer (Canyon CF 7 Di2 spec)
cockpit.stem: 2021–2024: Canyon V21 alloy aerostem (an owner reports 90 mm stock on a size M), subject to the steerer recall; facelift: one-piece carbon CP0041 bar/stem. Owners have fitted non-Canyon stems, but Canyon has refused recall/fork warranty when a non-Canyon stem was fitted.
cockpit.pad_bolt_spacing: Profile Design A2/A3 armrest pattern (Ergo armrest: width steps 18.5 mm, reach steps 15 mm per Profile Design's Canyon guide)
cockpit.stack_system: Profile Design A3 risers under the pads: 30 mm as delivered on 2021–2024 bikes, 35 mm on the 2025 CF 7 and CF 8. Going higher, up to 80 mm, means buying an A3 riser kit.
cockpit.reach_system: The pads slide on the Profile Design bracket in 15 mm steps. The extensions are 22.2 mm round bars, cut or clamped to length. On the one-piece CP0041 bar, sizes M–XL are 15 mm longer than XS–S. For more reach: the Profile Design A3 Reach Extender on the 2025 bar, or a longer stem on 2021–2024 bikes (Canyon has refused warranty claims on bikes fitted with a non-Canyon stem).
cockpit.angle_system: 0–15° stepless with the bracket bolts. 18–30° with the Profile Design A2 Tilt Booster on the 2025 bar.
cockpit.notes: Profile Design says its Reach Extender and Tilt Booster have not been tested with the 2021–2024 HB0053 base bar. Canyon will not sell the facelift cockpit for pre-facelift R073 frames. Canyon e-mailed Speedmax owners in July 2026 that untested third-party reach extenders/adapters may void the warranty; a fitter on Slowtwitch read the Profile Design reach extender as the common option for the CF.

stock_range.note: 2021-era Speedmax CF 8 Disc Di2 (V21 + HB0053 cockpit). Canyon does not state the pad measuring point.
Current CF 7 Di2 with CP0041 one-piece bar; 650b wheels on XS.

effect.text: A3 risers (5/10/20/40 mm pairs) + 5 mm bridge, up to 80 mm total versus 30–35 mm stock: roughly +45–50 mm of pad height.

evidence.says: Profile Design's Canyon upgrade guide lists 'A3 High' as the riser upgrade for Speedmax CF 2021–2024 and CF 7/CF 8 2025; max height 80 mm; full stack range needs an A3 riser kit.

parts.needs: Longer bolts included (75–100 mm). On A2 risers needs the A2-to-A3 adaptor.

effect.text: A3 risers + 40 mm carbon bridge, up to 60 mm total versus 30–35 mm stock.

evidence.says: Profile Design lists the A3C riser kit (max 60 mm) in the upgrade path for Speedmax CF 2021–2024 and 2025.

parts.model: Profile Design Speedmax CF Riser Kit (Canyon 10006304)

effect.text: Two 40 mm risers + 5 mm bridge with M6 bolts 70–100 mm.

evidence.says: Canyon: made for the Speedmax CF, works with Profile Design Sonic Ergo 35A extensions; contents named 'Aeria Ultimate Race Bracket Riser Kit'; GBP 9.99, sold out.
2021 Speedmax CF 8 Disc Di2 ships with Profile Design 35A extensions on the HB0053 base bar.

parts.needs: Sold out at Canyon GB. Canyon US sells a different kit (143422) for the rim-era H30 bar.

effect.text: Moves the arm pads about 30 mm forward (Profile Design guide; retailers quote 32 mm) and adds 25 mm of height.

evidence.says: Profile Design's Pad XY chart for CF 7/CF 8 (CP0041 bar) shows the most forward positions using the A3 Reach Extender; it notes the HB0053 bar (2021–2024) is untested with the Reach Extender.
Fitter names the PD reach extender as the usual reach part for the CF models.

parts.needs: On 2021–2024 HB0053 bikes Profile Design has not tested it; on A2 risers needs the A2-to-A3 adaptor; longer bolts.

effect.text: Adds 15° to the A2 bracket: 18–30° instead of 0–15°. Riser height 20.5 mm.

evidence.says: Guide: the bracket gives 0–15° natively, 18–30° with the A2 Tilt Booster (CF 7/CF 8, CP0041 bar); not tested on the HB0053 bar.
Product page: +15° for the A2 system, 18–30°, 20.5 mm riser height, USD 63.50; mixing non-PD parts may void warranty.

parts.needs: Untested by Profile Design on the 2021–2024 HB0053 bar.

effect.text: Higher-rise extensions than stock (52 ASC: 400 mm, 52° bend, 137 mm rise; ASC Pro: 325/350/375 mm, 43° on a 15° base, 146 mm rise vs 87 mm on the 52A).

evidence.says: Upgrade path for Speedmax CF 2021–2024 and 2025: 52 ASA, 52 ASC, ASC Pro extensions on the stock bracket.

parts.needs: ASC Pro is for Di2/AXS wireless shifting only.

effect.text: Alternative arm cups on the same bracket; change cup shape and width, not the stack/reach range.

evidence.says: Profile Design lists Ergo+, Race+ and Race-H armrests as upgrades for Speedmax CF 2021–2024 and 2025.

parts.model: Aerium C:68 base bar/stem with Profile Design fitting kit

effect.text: Replaces V21 stem + clip-ons with a one-piece aero bar on the standard 1-1/8 steerer; owner says the pads moved considerably forward and the front end is stiffer. No numbers given.

evidence.says: Owner of an R073 Speedmax CF (V21) fitted a Cube Aerium bar (~EUR 200) and Cube kit (~EUR 230); tracks better and stiffer.
Same owner, 3 months on: no compatibility issues, stem 18° drop; rear hose routed between Canyon spacer and stem.

parts.needs: Cube bracket/fitting kit, brake hose rerouting, a 3 mm spacer on the Canyon base spacer. Hard to source outside Europe. Canyon has refused recall warranty on bikes with non-Canyon stems.

parts.model: CP0041 one-piece carbon cockpit (2024 facelift) on a pre-facelift R073

effect.text: Retrofitting the newer Canyon bar to a 2021–2024 bike.

parts.reason_incompatible: Canyon told an owner the older frame is incompatible and would not sell the parts; another owner found the old fork crown has no channel for the new internal hose routing.

evidence.says: Canyon said the frame is incompatible and refused to sell the newer bar, fork or the HB0053.
Owner: no space in the old fork crown for internal routing; new bikes have a moulded channel.

parts.model: Speedmax Angle Fitting Kit / Monogrip Extension (CFR/SLX parts)

effect.text: Canyon's reach/tilt kit and mono extension for the CFR/CF SLX spacer column.

parts.reason_incompatible: Canyon lists both only for the Speedmax CFR (R085) and CF SLX (R091); the CF uses a Profile Design bracket on a standard base bar.

evidence.says: Angle Fitting Kit compatibility: Speedmax CFR and SLX (R085, R91).
Monogrip compatibility: Speedmax SLX (R091) and CFR (R085) only.

effect.text: Angle/reach spacer made for the CFR/CF SLX spacer column.

parts.reason_incompatible: Maker lists it only for disc-brake Speedmax SLX/CFR; the CF has a Profile Design riser/bracket system instead of Canyon's spacer column.

evidence.says: Compatibility given as Canyon Speedmax SLX/CFR with disc brakes.
Fitter pairs Radsport Ibert with the CF SLX/CFR and the PD reach extender with the CF models.

gaps: No published pad reference point for either armpad table; 2021 and current tables differ a lot (2021 reach span ~111 mm, stack span 70 mm; current 80 / 94 mm), so they are listed separately.
TriRig Alpha One was reported on rim-brake Speedmax CF bikes (2017–2020) and on a V21 Speedmax CF of unstated year; no report confirmed on a disc R073, so it is not listed.
Aftermarket longer stems (e.g. a 130 mm stem on an M) reported by owners of V21-era CF bikes, model year not stated; Canyon's stance on non-Canyon stems for warranty is strict (owners' screenshots).
Canyon 'Speedmax CF Spacer Kit for Triathlon Stem' (117059, +20 mm stem height, workshop fitting) does not state which CF years it fits; not listed.
Profile Design guide lists the 2025 CF 7 handlebar both as CP0041 and as 'Wing 20C 38cm' on different pages; Canyon's current CF 7 page says CP0041.
Profile Design product pages for A3 riser kits, A3 Reach Extender and ASC extensions not opened (rate-limited); prices not collected.
Pad width limits on the CF not quantified from a source.
